finding: Measured home gateways draw about twice the EU target: 13.8 W for a new US integrated gateway in 2025 against 6 to 8 W in the EU Code of Conduct, and the weighted average has stayed between 10 and 12.6 W for eleven years while speeds rose elevenfold. Routers and access points rose 20 % in one year (8.45 to 10.15 W) with Wi-Fi 7.
corrections: CORRECTION 2026-11-11 (same day as version 1): the fixed-network baseload rows from Carbon Trust 2021 (5 W access + 1.5 W core per line) are about right for copper and several times too high for fibre. The French regulator's reported figure is 20 kWh per subscription a year (about 2.3 W), under 10 kWh on fibre. Both are kept; use the regulator's for a status quo and say which technology.
arithmetic_for_the_consumer: From the 2012 LTE measurement: a small exchange every 5 minutes costs about 1 Wh a day on LTE and about 0.003 Wh on Wi-Fi. An exchange every 30 seconds with an 11.6 s tail keeps the radio in its high-power tail about 39 % of the time, about 0.4 W, about 10 Wh a day: most of a phone battery. This is arithmetic on one old handset, not a measurement of any current phone or of the mesh.
